name: Serragiumenta Castle
region: Calabria — Firmo, near Altomonte, Cosenza Province
architectural_style: Tied to the Sangineto family (early 14th century to 1381), then the Sanseverino (four centuries); a 16th-17th century residence with towers and two grand staircases on the main facade; agricultural estate founded in 1947
best_season: Year-round; spring and autumn for the Pollino foothills
accessibility: Accommodation is spread across the castle itself, a nearby agriturismo building, and glamping units among the vineyards; contact the estate directly regarding specific accessibility requirements.
tagline: A 16th-century Calabrian residence at the foot of Pollino National Park, held for over five centuries by the Sangineto and Sanseverino families
highlights: Tied to the Sangineto and Sanseverino families, who ruled the area for more than five combined centuries
Located at the foot of Pollino National Park, one of Italy's largest national parks
Rooftop swimming pool with panoramic views over the Calabrian hills
description:
The history of the Serragiumenta area and castle is tied to the Sangineto family, who ruled from the early 14th century until 1381, when the Sanseverino family began a four-century reign. Serragiumenta Castle is a magical place where an elegant garden frames a 16th-century residence, its towers and two prestigious staircases on the main facade enhancing its beauty.

More recently, the agricultural enterprise was founded in 1947 out of the passion of Federico Bilotti, and today carries a century-old history tied to the land and its produce. Located in the Altomonte area, in the heart of the Calabrian hills, at the foot of Pollino National Park and on the edge of the Sibari Plain, the castle today combines accommodation, agriculture, and rural tourism.

The successive five-century rule of the Sangineto and Sanseverino families ties Serragiumenta to the broader feudal history of Calabria, a region whose noble dynasties often held power over vast rural territories for far longer stretches than their counterparts in the more politically fragmented central and northern Italian city-states.

The 1947 founding of the agricultural enterprise by Federico Bilotti marks a deliberate 20th-century pivot from aristocratic residence to working farm, a transition that gives Serragiumenta a genuinely productive rural identity alongside its historic architecture.

The estate's position at the edge of the Sibari Plain connects it to the site of ancient Sybaris, one of the wealthiest and most legendarily luxurious cities of Magna Graecia, giving the surrounding landscape a layer of classical history well beyond the castle's own medieval and early modern story.

The accommodation split across the castle, a separate agriturismo building, and glamping units among the vineyards reflects the estate's broader identity as a working rural tourism operation rather than a single-purpose historic hotel.
history: Serragiumenta Castle's history is tied to the Sangineto family (early 14th century to 1381) and then the Sanseverino, who ruled for four centuries. The residence, built in the 16th-17th century with towers and grand staircases, sits at the foot of Pollino National Park. In 1947, Federico Bilotti founded the agricultural enterprise that today combines the historic castle with a working farm, agriturismo, and glamping accommodation.

faqs.question: Are all the rooms at Serragiumenta Castle within the historic building?
faqs.answer: No — only 7 suites (upper floor) and 4 apartments (ground floor) are within the 17th-century castle itself. There are also 6 rooms in a nearby agriturismo building (not part of the castle) and 3 glamping units among the vineyards.

faqs.question: What families held Serragiumenta Castle historically?
faqs.answer: The Sangineto family from the early 14th century until 1381, followed by the Sanseverino family, who ruled the area for four centuries.

faqs.question: What is Serragiumenta Castle close to?
faqs.answer: Pollino National Park, one of Italy's largest national parks, and the Sibari Plain with its ancient Greek archaeological sites.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** About 15 minutes from Altomonte and 45 minutes from Cosenza by car; Lamezia Terme Airport (SUF) is about 1h30 away.

**Rooms & rates:** 7 suites on the upper floor of the 17th-century castle, 4 apartments on the ground floor, 6 rooms in a nearby agriturismo (not in the castle), and 3 glamping units among the vineyards. From €108/night.

**On-site:** Rooftop pool, large garden and terrace, restaurant, agritourism activities.

**Good to know:** If you specifically want to sleep inside the 17th-century castle, book one of the 7 suites or 4 apartments — the other options (agriturismo, glamping) are outside the historic building.

**Combine with:** Altomonte (~15 min), Pollino National Park, the Sibari Plain and its ancient Greek archaeological sites.
